correctness.rationale: The published scalar theorem fixes optimum weight four. The proof then exhausts the only three possible positive-label multisets at weight four. Two label-2 vertices must lie on opposite sides and must both be universal. A 2+1+1 labeling forces the defender's side to have order two and its defender to be universal; the all-one labeling forces total order four. Every listed family directly satisfies both quasi-total Roman conditions. A standalone verifier checked every ternary labeling of 114 connected canonical chain-graph types of total order four through eight.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete optimization-solution classification for a standard graph class on which only the scalar optimum and an algorithm were previously known. The count collapses to four explicit families controlled only by the universal twin classes and the two side sizes. It yields concrete consequences such as uniqueness on every half graph H_n for n at least three and also supplies the universally valid construction behind the published scalar theorem.
